candidate.proposed_question: When may the State Commission transfer a complaint pending before a District Commission to another District Commission in the State?
candidate.proposed_answer: On the complainant's application or on its own motion, the State Commission may transfer such a complaint at any stage of the proceeding if the interest of justice so requires.
candidate.source_text_finding: Section 48 on the cited Consumer Act PDF page identifies the application/own-motion route, timing, transfer destination within the State, and interests-of-justice condition.
candidate.quality_or_scope_flags: The suggested question/answer capture the listed conditions; 'such a complaint' relies on the question for its referent.
candidate.source_provision_excerpt:
48. On the application of the complainant or of its own motion, the State Commission
may, at any stage of the proceeding, transfer any complaint pending before a District
Commission to another District Commission within the State if the interest of justice so
requires.
